aw ARM64 1.36.33 triage (Windows PE, Darwin Mach-O, Linux ELF)
Judgement: BENIGN for all three npm tarballs.

Previous release fetched from registry.npmjs.org: 1.36.32, published on
2026-10-10 before 1.36.33. Both versions on all three platforms match the
registry SHA-512 integrity. Package members remain two Go executables,
package.json and an empty .gitkeep; manifests differ only in version.
Source: https://github.com/awebai/aw/compare/v1.36.32...v1.36.33
Old commit: df6bb1936ab687614f483d514243601718728f7e
New commit: 877bbee94ce45aa1ff103912bc9850556e61dfb4

All three aw executables retain Go 1.24.13, dependency versions/checksums,
CGO settings, architecture and build flags. Changes match ordinary fixes:
- Authenticate received addressless senders against the selected team's
  registry and membership, rejecting mismatched identities and stale proofs.
- Persist authority-scoped verified identity-log checkpoints and reject
  rollback/forked checkpoints; preserve decrypted authenticated metadata.
- Canonicalize the custody working directory and propagate path errors.
- Serialize status writes and reuse an exclusively created private scratch
  filename, preventing symlink/clobber attacks and reducing VFS churn.
No new payload acquisition, secret export or unsolicited command execution.

Go pclntab comparison: exactly 10 additional functions in each aw executable.
The new application functions implement sender verification/checkpointing and
atomic status writes. Gateway additions implement the same identity handling.
The ordinary main-package digit-bearing function set is IDENTICAL in both
versions (30 Linux/Darwin candidates; 29 Windows). Thus the immediately prior
release does not substantiate a new obfuscation change. Under the current
heuristic these existing protocol names are already false-positive evidence.
Examples: main.buildA2ACardOutput, main.verifyA2ACardWithAWID,
main.configureClientE2EEForRead, main.e2eeEnvelopesEqual.

Deep inspection: rizin disassembly of Linux NormalizeReceivedSenderTrust at
0x38f740 confirms status comparisons and identity gating. e2eeEnvelopesEqual
at 0x709880 calls CanonicalJSONValue twice and compares the resulting bytes;
it is an ordinary envelope equality function. writeJSONAtomicWithTempName at
0x6c4b80 calls MkdirAll(0700), MarshalIndent, and either CreateTemp or
OpenFile with flags 0xc1 (WRONLY|CREATE|EXCL) and mode 0600. Recovered call
targets from pclntab agree with the corresponding source implementations.

Trait fix: filter A2A and E2EE protocol acronyms from matched identifier
candidates in go-garbled-main-digit, using per-evidence not: rather than a
product/version exemption or whole-file exclusion. Preserve real random
identifiers elsewhere in the same binary. Threshold and severity unchanged.

Focused compiled Go controls (Linux ARM64, stripped, no inline functions):
- Eight random alphanumeric main names: atom and suspicious composite MATCH.
- Eight A2A/E2EE names: atom and suspicious composite DO NOT MATCH.
- Eight random names plus eight A2A/E2EE names: both still MATCH.
Full atomscan reruns and cleave facts were performed for all three tarballs;
executable facts, upstream tarballs, source diff and resolved disassembly are
in the session scratch/aw-triage directory, outside this traits repository.

Final scans: Windows, Darwin and Linux archives, both executables, manifests
and registry records all have 0 hostile and 0 suspicious traits. All three
archive ML levels are -1 (benign). The random-name controls still detect.
